Here's a concise, step-by-step guide to setting up and maintaining a square-foot garden the right way:

| Step | What to Do | Why It Matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **1. Choose Your Bed Size** | Build or buy a raised bed, typically 4x4 feet.<br>• Keep it narrow enough to reach the center from any side. | A compact bed keeps the whole garden reachable without stepping on the soil. |
| **2. Pick a Sunny Spot** | Place the bed where it gets at least 6 hours of direct sun.<br>• Avoid low spots that collect water. | Most vegetables need full sun to produce well. |
| **3. Prepare the Soil Mix | • Base Mix:** ⅔ topsoil + ⅓ compost | A light, fertile mix drains well and feeds seedlings without added fertilizer. |
| **4. Add the Grid** | Divide the bed into 1-foot squares with string or wood strips.<br>• One square per crop type. | The grid is what makes square-foot spacing easy to follow at a glance. |

### Quick Tips for Success

- Water consistently, about 1 inch per week.
- Rotate crops each season to keep the soil balanced.
- Thin seedlings early so each square isn't overcrowded.
